codeReview.summary: The commit fixes displayed path formatting for the parity scenario, but it regresses `-g` filename-regex matching semantics by matching against normalized paths instead of baseline raw paths; this violates the feature's no-regression requirement.

issues.description: `-g` regex matching now runs on `display_path_for(f)` (normalized output path) via `file_re.is_match(&display)`. Baseline ag matches against raw `dir_full_path` (`src/search.c:629`) and only normalizes when printing (`src/print.c:361`). Regression evidence: `./ag --nocolor --workers=1 --parallel --noaffinity -g '^\./rust-ag/src/main\.rs$' foo .` prints `rust-ag/src/main.rs` and exits 0, while `target/debug/rust-ag --nocolor --workers=1 --parallel --noaffinity -g '^\./rust-ag/src/main\.rs$' foo .` exits 1 with no stdout.

New tests added for this fix assert only that output lines do not start with `./`, but they use absolute temp-dir paths (`run_ag(&["-g", "\.rs$", dir_path])`) and do not exercise `.`-rooted paths or `-g` regex matching semantics. They would not catch the blocking regression above.

sharedStateObservations.observation: CLI formatting tests for `-g` can pass while changing filename-regex semantics because they assert output formatting only; the test convention does not require semantic guards for regex matching against raw vs normalized paths.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: manifests/scenarios.json:345-352 defines `cli-filename-filter-g` with corpus `.` and pattern placeholder; rust-ag/tests/parity_cli_context_color_filters.rs:404-452 only checks prefix formatting on temp-dir outputs.

sharedStateObservations.observation: `rewrite-worker` mandates red-first tests, but this run edited implementation before adding new tests; skill feedback still marked followedProcedure=true.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Skill requirement at .factory/skills/rewrite-worker/SKILL.md:19; transcript skeleton (worker-transcripts.jsonl line 37) shows `Tool: Edit` on `rust-ag/src/main.rs` before the later step 'Now let me add a test for this specific behavior.'

sharedStateObservations.observation: A critical baseline nuance is undocumented in shared library docs: `-g` regex is evaluated on raw paths, while printed paths are normalized separately. Missing this nuance makes regressions likely in future path-format fixes.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Baseline behavior in src/search.c:629 (`pcre_exec(... dir_full_path ...)`) and src/print.c:361 (`normalize_path` before printing); no matching guidance found in .factory/library/*.md for `normalize_path` or `-g` path-matching semantics.

summary: Review failed: output formatting parity was fixed, but the implementation now matches `-g` regex against normalized display paths, breaking baseline-compatible filename-filter semantics for patterns that depend on leading `./`.
